message.content:
**Proteins commonly found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Function | Representative Examples | |----------|------------------|-------------------------| | **Integral (Trans‑membrane)** | Span the bilayer; form pores/transport pathways or signal transduction sites | • Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase
• Glucose transporter GLUT1
• Aquaporin‑2
• Voltage‑gated K⁺ channel Kv11.1
• G‑protein–coupled receptors (e.g., β₂‑adrenergic)
• Connexin43 (gap junctions)
• Caveolin‑1 (caveolae scaffold) | | **Peripheral / Loops** | Attach to one leaflet via hydrophilic interactions; often link to cytoskeleton or signaling complexes | • Integrin α5β1 (extracellular matrix adhesion)
• Cadherin E-cadherin (homophilic cell–cell adhesion)
• Receptor tyrosine kinases (EGFR – usually anchored through a short TM segment plus extracellular domain)
• Scaffold proteins (PSD‑95, ankyrin‑R) | | **Lipid‑anchored** | Covalently attached to lipids rather than spanning the membrane | • Squalene synthase (prenylation)
• Hedgehog family members (cholesterol‑modified)
• Protein kinase Cα (phosphatidylserine binding) | | **Extracellular Matrix Proteoglycan Anchors** | Bind ECM components while remaining tethered to the surface | • Versican core protein (via GPI anchor)
• Perlecan (heparan sulfate proteoglycan) | ### Quick Highlights * **Ion Channels & Transporters:** * Sodium/potassium pump (maintains electrochemical gradients). * Aquaporins (water selective channels). * **Transporter Receptors:** * Glucose transporters (GLUT family). * Amino acid carriers (LAT1). * **Signal Transducers:** * GPCRs (odorant receptors, chemokine receptors). * RTKs (Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor). * **Cell Adhesion Molecules:** * Cadherins (tissue integrity). * Integrins (ECM attachment, focal adhesions). * **Gap Junction Components:** * Connexins forming intercellular channels. * **Structural Scaffolds:** * Caveolins organizing cholesterol‑rich microdomains (“lipid rafts”). * Cytoplasmic adaptors linking membrane proteins to actin filaments (ankyrin, spectrin). These proteins together give the plasma membrane its dynamic roles—selective permeability, communication between cells, mechanical support, and interaction with the external environment.
